function: Excluded, function. p. 10: the learned KSGAN discriminator only detects adversarial attacks on radar Range-Doppler maps; ISAC power split and sensing beam follow fixed threshold rules (eqs. 22-23).
notes: Page 1 holds the title and DOI 10.1109/TVT.2025.3583924, so the PDF is this paper. Step 1: a research article (not code 1) that proposes and evaluates a method (not 2); learning is central (p. 9: "To detect AML attacks, we designed a unique GAN that is trained with a differentiable KS loss function"), so not 3; the learning acts on the radar Range-Doppler map, not above the PHY (not 4). Code 5 applies: the learned model only classifies Range-Doppler maps as real or adversarial (p. 10: "The discriminator is tasked with detecting whether there is an AML attack"; Fig. 5, p. 9), a security function akin to the excluded physical-layer authentication and anti-jamming. No learned component outputs beams, waveforms, or resources: the sensing/communication power split and the sensing-beam on/off are fixed threshold rules on the detector output (p. 10, eqs. 22-23; p. 12, eq. 25), the communication precoder is closed form (p. 5: "We employ Regularized Zero-Forcing (RZF) precoding"), the mode-switch period comes from a Poisson model (p. 12), and range and velocity come from classical 2D CFAR (p. 6). Borderline for the reviewer: the paper casts detection as subproblem P1a of a weighted-CRLB resource problem (p. 8) and the detector output gates the ISAC transmission, so area 5 could be argued; I judged that the ISAC resource decision itself is not learned. Not graded.
